Challenging impugned judgment and awarded dated 15.02.2016 passed by Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T, Kundgol, in MVC no.670/2015 these appeals are filed.

entities.text: Basappa Basavraj S/O Bagigeppa vs Smt Neelawwa Koppad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Brief facts as stated are that on 20.02.2015, Sankappa was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KA.25/ED-5496 from Kundgol to Hirenarti.
Near Benakanahalli, rider of another motorcycle bearing registration KA-26/ER-8318 carrying two pillion riders and riding it in rash and negligent manner, dashed against motorcycle.
As result Sankappa sustained grievous injuries.
Due to which he died during treatment at KIMS Hospital, Hubli on 20.02.2015.
Claiming compensation on account of his untimely death, his wife filed claim petition against owner and insurer of offending vehicle under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
C/W 3.

On contest, wherein claim petition was opposed on all counts including alleging entire negligence against deceased himself, tribunal framed issues and thereafter recorded evidence of claimant as P.W.1 and marked Exs.P.1 to 14.
In rebuttal, official of insurer was examined as R.W.1 and Exs.R.1 to R5 were marked.

4. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider and insurance policy was duly issued and claimants were entitled for compensation of Rs.5,15,111/- with interest at rate of 6% per annum.
But taking note of fact that rider of offending motorcycle was carrying two pillion riders, liability of insurer was absolved and fastened on owner.
Assailing owner has filed MFA no.100361/2023, while seeking for enhancement of compensation MFA no.100478/2017 is filed by claimant.
C/W 5.

Sri . N.L.Batakurki, learned counsel for owner submitted that only reason assigned by tribunal for discharging liability of insurer and holding owner liable was that at time of accident, insured vehicle was carrying two pillion riders in violation of Section 128 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Relying upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of MOHAMMED SIDDIQUE AND OTHERS VS.
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in (2020) 3 SCC 57, it was submitted that Hon'ble Supreme Court had held that unless it was case of insurer that accident occurred only due to rider of motorcycle was carrying two pillion riders, liability could not be fastened upon owner.

entities.text:
MOHAMMED SIDDIQUE AND OTHERS VS.
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in (2020) 3 SCC 57
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that there must be causal connection between violation and accident or due to same contributing to gravity of injuries.
In absence of same, it would not be proper to hold that there would be violation of policy conditions discharging liability of insurer.
C/W 6.

Sri.C.M.Hosamani, learned counsel for claimant/appellants submitted that though deceased in instant case was 48 years and earning Rs.15,000/- per month from agriculture, tribunal erroneously considered his monthly income at Rs.4,500/- per month and sought enhancement.
It was further submitted that tribunal also erred in not adding future prospects to income.
7. Sri. A.G.Jadhav, learned counsel for respondent/insurer opposed both appeals.

It was submitted that in Police investigation records, it was clearly mentioned that rider of insured vehicle was Basappa Basavraj S/O Bagigeppa vs Smt Neelawwa Koppad on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140301667/
4 carrying two pillion riders.

entities.text: Basappa Basavraj S/O Bagigeppa vs Smt Neelawwa Koppad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While passing impugned judgment, tribunal had assessed evidence on record and as same was in violation of Section 128 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, rightly discharged liability of insurer.
It was further submitted that claimant failed to lead any specific evidence regarding his monthly C/W income.
In absence, tribunal rightly assessed it notionally and same did not call for any interference.
On above grounds sought for dismissal of appeals.

8. Heard learned counsel for both parties, perused impugned judgment and award.
9.

From above submission, since owner is in appeal while challenging discharge of liability of insurer and claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation, following points would arise for consideration:
" 1 . Whether finding of tribunal discharging liability of insurer calls for interference?"
"2. Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
10. Point no.1:
There is no dispute about insured motorcycle was with two pillion riders at time C/W of accident.

However, whether said fact contributed to accident or was sole reason for accident has to be determined has held that by Hon'ble Supreme Court in MOHAMMED SIDDIQUE's (supra).
11.
In ordered to verify same, I have perused objections filed by insurer.

In objections, insurer has mainly objected on ground of violation of Section 128 of Motor Vehicles Act, and has not specifically contended that only due to carriage of two pillion riders, rider of insured vehicle unable to control and same resulted in accident.
It is also not specific case of insurer that gravity of injuries sustained were aggravated.

Even in cross examination of claimant, there are no specific suggestions are elicitation to this fact in any case no specific evidence led by insurer to establish that carriage of two pillion riders contributed or was sole cause for accident.
Under such circumstances and in view of legal position arriving from MOHAMMED SIDDIQUE's case, finding of tribunal would be justified and same does calls for interference.

Hence,
point no.1 is answered in affirmative.
It is held that insurer would be liable to pay compensation.
13. Point no.2:
Insofar as monthly income though claimant stated that deceased was aged about 40 years, working as agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/- per month, same is not substantiated.
In absence of same, income has to be assessed notionally.

Notional income for year 2015 is Rs.8,000/-
per month.
Therefore, tribunal was justified in taking it at Rs.8,000 /-.
Claimant is wife of deceased and sole dependent.

Though learned counsel for claimant submitted that deceased was married,
deduction towards 'personal expenses' should be 1/3rd in para 30 of its decision in SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS VS.

5 - 11 -  C/W DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in [2009] 6 SCC 121-, same was affirmed in PRANAY SETHI case, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as follows:
30.

entities.text:
SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS VS.
Basappa Basavraj S/O Bagigeppa vs Smt Neelawwa Koppad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though in some cases the deduction to be made towards personal and living expenses is calculated on the basis of units indicated in Trilok Chandra [(1996) 4 SCC 362] , the general practice is to apply standardised deductions.

Having considered several subsequent decisions of this Court, we are of the view that where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased,
should be one- third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, one-fourth (1/4th) where the number of dependent family members is 4 to 6, and one-fifth (1/5th) where the number of dependent family members exceeds six.
(Emplasis supplied)
14. Therefore, deduction towards 'personal expenses' would have to be at 50%.
However tribunal has erred in not adding future prospects.

15. Thus, loss of dependency would have to be reassessed as follows:
 Rs.8,000/- + 25% -1/2 x 12 x 13 =Rs.7,80,000/-
 - 12 -  C/W  16.
Apart from above, claimant would be entitled for Rs.70,000/- under 'conventional heads' and addition of 10% on award under conventional heads i.e Rs.7,000/-(Rs.70,000/- x 10%).
Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,111/- towards 'medical expenses' since Sankappa claimant died during treatment.

Therefore, claimant would Basappa Basavraj S/O Bagigeppa vs Smt Neelawwa Koppad on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140301667/
6 entitled for same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus claimant would be entitled for total compensation as follows:
Sl.no.

Heads Amount  1 Loss of dependency 7,80,000/-
 2 Conventional heads 70,000/-
 3 Additional 10% under 7,000/-
 conventional Heads

4 Medical expenses 2,111/-
 Total 8,59,111/-
17.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative as above.
18. Consequently, I pass following - 13 - C/W ORDER.
a) MFA no.100361/2023 is allowed.
Award of tribunal fastening liability on owner is set aside and insurer is held liable to pay compensation.
b) Amount in deposit is ordered to be refunded to appellant.
c) MFA no.100478/2017 is allowed in part.
Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.8,59,111/- with interest at rate of 6% per annum.
d) Insurer is directed deposit same within six weeks.
e) Directions issued by tribunal regarding deposit and release shall be apply to reassessed enhanced compensation also.

Sd/-
